column1: # Expected test count per filtered CI lane. Regenerate: scripts/assert-lane-counts.sh --update
# EXACT: a lane that grows OR shrinks fails until this file is updated in the same change.
# A floor let growth accumulate as slack a later deletion could hide inside.
# 2026-09-27: every durability lane but wal-and-snapshot-chaos counts with --run-ignored only, the
# mode it now runs with; these rows used to count --run-ignored all whatever the lane ran. Every
# test that left a lane is non-ignored in a package whose railgun-tests shard runs it under the
# same ci-test cargo profile, and the two terms that selected nothing under only were dropped.
durability-and-closure/wal-and-snapshot-chaos
# 2026-09-27: cli-ignored lost the three tests of the `[[ppoi_list_template]]` auto-spawn, deleted
# with it: it spawned only whole-list instances, which the mirror never fed.
durability-and-closure/cli-ignored
durability-and-closure/shipped-config-spawn
# Its filter carries a bare `test(insert_rejects_overflow_past_capacity)` that resolves to an
# in-src lib test. The original anchor counted only `pkg::binary test` rows and silently dropped
# every in-src test, undercounting the one lane whose filter depends on one.
# The number lives in the row below and nowhere else; state the reason here, never the value.
# 2026-09-28: 2 -> 1. engine_dedup_extends_to_encoder lost its one ignored test, which booted two
# whole-list instances of different per-list encoders; neither that route nor a second per-list
# encoder exists, and the binary left this lane's filter with it.
durability-and-closure/engine-ignored
# 2026-09-28: 6 -> 4. t1_status_closure and t2_path_closure were deleted with the status and
# per-list-path encoders they closed; their terms left the filter in the same change.
durability-and-closure/closure
# 2026-09-07: was 21 before wave 5. binary(db2_block_production_cell) lost
# block_exponent_and_payload_are_pinned_to_the_read_path_design, which asserted BLOCK_K == 10
# against a `const BLOCK_K: usize = 10` three lines above it in the same test file; verified no
# production symbol carries BLOCK_K, so no shipped-code change could ever red it. A sibling test
# was FOLDED (its subtree-root assert moved into the splice loop, which visits all three block
# indices). The count also moved because this gate's row anchor was corrected the same day: it
# had missed nextest's lib-target rows (`pkg imt::tests::x`, no `::` before the space) and then,
# briefly, its bench rows (`pkg::bench/name x`, a slash in the binary segment).
# 2026-09-22: 23 -> 34 -> 40. The lane gained the `raven-railgun-http` package and a
# `binary(poi_shim_coverage)` term, for one test that seeds five sealed 65,536-row blocks and so
# cannot run per push. The other tests in that binary come along. The pin is
# raised rather than left low because a floor below the truth cannot detect a drop (the ratchet
# was a floor then; it is exact now, so growth fails too). 34 was exact when set (that binary had
# 11 tests); the index-channel work took it to 17, so the lane now selects 40. Counted with the
# gate's own row regex, not estimated. Bump this in the SAME change that adds tests to any binary
# the filter names.
# 2026-09-24: +1, a CORS test proving a cross-origin reader sees every index-cursor header.
# 2026-09-25: +4. poi_shim_coverage proves a short or empty frontier is answered only while upstream's
# own recent row count vouches for it (a cold sync part-way, and an empty block over sealed ones), that
# a block declared ahead of the list is answered over while a row past an empty block is a hole, and
# that each list is answered only on its own upstream count.
# 2026-09-27: 47 -> 46. populate_bench left with the synthetic PPOI server it timed; its one test
# fed a PPOI list through a commit-tree encoder, which measures nothing the forest serves.
# 2026-09-27: 46 -> 37. poi_shim_coverage lost the tests of the removed JSON index and
# per-commitment status routes and of the undeclared single-store path, and folded two duplicates
# into the index-channel tests. Its fixtures now seed a sealed block as one run: about 1.7 s per
# test that seeds one, and 8.3 s for the five-block test, measured under ci-test. The earlier
# "cheap" was wrong: each of those tests then seeded its own sealed block at about 33 s.
production-cell-closure/inline
